claims.text: Signed 'DWIGHT D. EISENHOWER / THE WHITE HOUSE / November 5, 1953', effective 15 December 1953 under section 20.
Section 19: 'Executive Order No. 10290 of September 24, 1951 is revoked as of the effective date of this order.'
Section 1 fixes exactly three categories, Top Secret, Secret and Confidential, and bars any other designation for defense information 'except as expressly provided by statute.'

claims.source: EO 10501 sec. 2 and attached memorandum, https://irp.fas.org/offdocs/eo10501.htm
claims.text: IT TOOK CLASSIFICATION AUTHORITY AWAY, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE DIRECTION THE SYSTEM LATER TRAVELLED. Section 2, 'Limitation of Authority to Classify', provides that for agencies with no direct national-defense responsibility 'there shall be no authority for original classification of information or material under this order', and limits agencies with partial responsibility to the agency head without delegation. The attached memorandum names 28 agencies stripped of the authority, including the Federal Trade Commission, the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Veterans Administration, and 17 more limited to the agency head alone.

THE JOIN TO THE NUCLEAR REGIME. Section 13 expressly leaves Atomic Energy Act Restricted Data outside the order's reach. The executive classification system and the statutory Restricted Data system are two systems, and the executive one says so.

The Federal Register citation usually given for this order, 18 FR 7049, was NOT verified. federalregister.gov redirects this environment to a bot-block page, and the text read was a transcription hosted elsewhere.

connections.edgeLabel: Excludes Restricted Data from the executive classification system
connections.label: Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (Pub. L. 83-703, 68 Stat. 919)
connections.note: Section 13 leaves Atomic Energy Act Restricted Data outside the order's reach. This is the seam between the two regimes: one body of information in United States law is classified by statute and not by executive order, and the executive order says so itself. Note the order predates the 1954 Act by ten months and the exclusion runs to the Atomic Energy Act as it then stood.

timeline.label: EO 10501 fixes three classification levels and strips 28 agencies of the power to classify
timeline.text: Eisenhower signs EO 10501, effective 15 December 1953, revoking EO 10290 of 1951. It limits defense-information markings to Top Secret, Secret and Confidential, removes original classification authority entirely from 28 named agencies and limits 17 more to the agency head. Section 13 leaves Atomic Energy Act Restricted Data outside the order, which is where the two classification regimes part company.
